Every control is a composition from tokens, named '<CMP id> <Name> (composition)': the wireframes are greys only, and cvsheet v1 cannot recolour an instance or swap its glyph.

Segmented controls draw the anatomy's words verbatim, the selected one in capitals as written (BUY, LIMIT; §5.1 L458, §6.1 L628) and marked by the selected fill; the unit switch's '*' (L330) is that fill.

The levels table is drawn in its monospaced form by default: each row one JetBrains Mono text whose columns are space-padded (numbers right-aligned, 'where' left), as the spec's own sketches draw it (§5.1 L464-469, §5.2), so a whole SCR-065 frame fits one section (FRAME_NOTE); the padding is U+00A0, so Penpot keeps it (live check: the columns align); mono=False draws one text per cell.
Frame captions, annotation labels, board titles, source lines and footers are board chrome, not product copy.
1 px outlines use cvlib's default stroke (1 px, inner) without binding border.hairline; 2 px boundaries and rings bind border.thick / border.focus (frames stay small: FRAME_NOTE).

Modal sizes are kit choices (the spec gives none): SCR-064 640 px wide, SCR-065 800 px (its minimum width 640 px collapses notional and cum. notional, §5.2 L519), SCR-069 720 px; heights hug the content except the 50-row frame (12 body rows, §5.2 L527).
No close (×) control is drawn in the dialog headers: §3.1 L152 names the verb, the object and the environment pill only; Esc closes (L151).

Every number is JetBrains Mono (§3.1 L155) in fields, cells, tiles and the read-out pairs; a number inside a sentence keeps the sentence's Inter, because a cvsheet v1 text node carries one typography.
A focus ring is a 2 px inner stroke on a wrapper with space.inset.xs padding, so it sits 2 px off the control and adds 4 px on each side to the layout (CMP-039).
A validity hold (§3.6 L250-252: 'the host's call') is drawn as the control's own look with its reason as a description and no lock glyph: the spec does not draw it.

Frames are named 'SCR-0xx / <state>' (§0 L47), and cvsheet splits section paths on '/', so no section can address a node inside a frame: every frame is rendered whole in one section (the kit keeps each under 24000 bytes; one over the 12000-byte budget is listed in live_checks).
